name: Mockchats
tagline: Builds fake iMessage, WhatsApp and Instagram DM conversations and exports them as clean screenshots or clips for ads, thumbnails and story content.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: This is a form, a styled chat bubble list, and a screenshot of a DOM node. There is no backend logic worth paying for: no network, no proprietary data, no integration surface, just CSS that looks like iOS and a PNG exporter. An agent can produce a working local version in one sitting, including the fiddly bits like read receipts, typing indicators, timestamps and status bar time. The honest gap is pixel fidelity: matching the exact San Francisco font metrics, bubble radii, and per-OS-version details is the actual craft here, and your first build will look like a chat app rather than a screenshot of one. If you need animated video output with per-message timing, that is a second day of work, not a second product.
coreLoopDIY: A local editor where you type a conversation script, pick a platform skin and phone frame, and export a retina PNG that looks like a real chat screenshot.
requirements: Legally obtained system fonts or free lookalikes for the iOS and Android UI text
Optional: ffmpeg if you want to stitch animated exports into video
whatYouLose: Pixel-accurate platform skins that someone maintains as iOS and WhatsApp keep redesigning
A library of ready avatars, wallpapers, and phone frames you did not have to source
Animated video export with per-message timing and sound, if the paid tool offers it
Bundled font licensing headaches handled by someone else
Sharing a template with a teammate or client without sending them a repo
moatNotes: The moat is that the fake looks real, which is a font and pixel problem, plus a stack of asset licenses you probably do not want to think about.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because the value is entirely in fidelity and speed, and a marketer making forty chat screenshots for ad variants does not want to debug why their bubble tails look wrong. A paid tool ships with the skins, the avatars, the wallpapers, and the correct fonts already sorted, and it updates when the platforms redesign. If you make two of these a year, build it. If you make two hundred, the subscription is cheaper than your evening.
notes: One of the rare cases where the whole product is CSS with good taste, and good taste is the only thing you cannot npm install.
prompt:
Build a local, single-user fake chat screenshot generator. No accounts, no backend, no telemetry, no cloud.

Stack, non-negotiable: Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS. State in a single Zustand store, persisted to localStorage. Use html-to-image for export. No server, no database, no external API calls.

Layout: two panes. Left is the editor, right is a live phone preview.

Editor pane:
- Conversation metadata: contact name, avatar (local file upload, stored as a data URL), platform skin, phone frame on/off, wallpaper (color or uploaded image), status bar time, battery percent, signal bars, dark mode toggle.
- Message list with add, delete, drag to reorder. Each message has: side (incoming/outgoing), text, optional image attachment, optional timestamp label shown above it, delivered/read status, and a reaction emoji.
- Special row types: typing indicator (three animated dots), date divider, and system line like "Missed call".
- A bulk script textarea that parses lines of the form "me: hey" and "them: hi" into messages, so a whole conversation can be pasted at once.

Preview pane:
- Three skins implemented as separate React components sharing a message model: iMessage (blue/gray bubbles, tails, SF-like font stack), WhatsApp (green outgoing, tick marks, wallpaper), Instagram DM (gradient outgoing bubbles, no tails).
- Render at a fixed logical width of 390px and scale with CSS transform so the export is crisp.

Export:
- Buttons for PNG at 1x, 2x, 3x, plus copy-to-clipboard. Export exactly the phone node, no editor chrome.
- A JSON export/import of the whole conversation so presets can be saved to disk.

Explicitly out of scope: video or animated GIF export, real messaging integrations, multi-user sharing, any hosted component. Do not bundle proprietary fonts; use a system font stack and add a README note about which fonts to install locally for accurate rendering.

Ship a README with run instructions and one seeded example conversation so the app is not empty on first load.
